fact: Submarine Networks (31 July 2025) states 2Africa has two Mozambique landing points, Maputo and Nacala, and that EASSy and SEACOM both land in Maputo, so a cable in service at Nacala is separate from those at Maputo.

Submarine Networks states that before 2Africa arrived only two international subsea cables connected Mozambique, EASSy and SEACOM, both landing in Maputo; the document gives no date, so its published date is used.

WIOCC and Tmcel signed a framework agreement on 23 July 2025 in Maputo under which WIOCC delivers capacity on the 2Africa East subsea cable and terrestrial routes into South Africa to Tmcel, as reported by Submarine Networks.
SDxCentral (15 August 2023) reports Vodacom said the 2Africa cable officially launched in Mozambique at Nacala-Porto, after landing in Maputo in February 2023; Vodacom is the project partner.

MoRENet's deck (30 October 2025) states its international capacity is 60 Gbps with active redundancy over two continental routes (Atlantic via a Cape Town PoP onto AmLight-SACS, and East African routes with IP transit via WIOCC); before this it had 5 Gbps over a single route through South Africa.
